title: SKU-aware burst bandwidth orchestrator with eviction budget watcher
creator: Marco Diaz
description: Implement an orchestration layer that assigns per-tenant burst budgets across heterogeneous GPU SKUs and regions, prefers cheaper spot capacity when safe, and gracefully degrades to cheaper model variants or lower throughput under hard budget pressure. This ticket implements the controller, API hooks, simulation harness, and an initial rollout strategy for low-risk tenants.
background: Current routing uses a single global spend governor that picks spot when available and falls back to on-demand. We lack a per-tenant burst allocation that understands SKU performance differences (FP16 vs INT8 quantized latency), regional price/eviction profiles, and model-variant quality trade-offs. This leads to either over-spend or excessive throttling and unpredictable user-facing latency spikes during regional scarcity.
technical_design: 1) Budget waterfall allocator: each tenant gets a steady-state allowance + burst window. Bursts consume a tiered pool: local-region cheap-spot pool -> cross-region cheap-spot pool -> on-demand local -> on-demand cross-region. Pools are tracked per SKU family (A100, H100, fractional-quantized variants) and decayed over sliding windows. 2) SKU affinity scoring: combine measured p95 latency, cost-per-token, and eviction-rate signal into a single score used by the router to select device class. 3) Variant fallback graph: precomputed compatibility graph that maps primary model -> lower-cost variants, with expected quality delta and token inflation factors. 4) Safety caps: soft caps trigger suggestions (prefetch KV, increase batching), hard caps cause deterministic degradation path (model variant, reduced concurrency). 5) API/Config: expose tenant-level budget caps, burst multipliers, and a "graceful-degrade policy" field. 6) Telemetry: add per-decision tags to traces and new metrics: budget_consumed, budget_remaining_window, fallback_events, sku_eviction_score.
tradeoffs: - Granularity vs complexity: tracking per-tenant-per-sku provides best decisions but increases metric cardinality and complexity in allocator. We start with per-tenant-per-region-per-sku-bucket (coarser) and can refine.\n- Quality vs cost: automatic fallbacks reduce spend but risk user-visible regressions; require prompt-level evals and opt-out.\n- Conservative default: to avoid customer surprise, defaults will bias toward preserving model quality and only apply aggressive degradations to tenants with explicit budget-caps enabled.
implementation_notes:
- Controller service will be a new subcomponent under routing: budget-orchestrator. Lightweight in-memory store with periodic reconciliation to central config store (etcd).
- Integrate with existing routing policy engine via a hook that returns (region, sku_family, model_variant, throttle_hint).
- Use existing eviction telemetry (spot-eviction-rate) and add short-lived probes: small synthetic requests to candidate SKUs to approximate tail latency under load. Probes run at low frequency and only for tenants opted-in.
- Simulation: create load generator that replays production request shape to validate budget depletion patterns before rollout.
- Backwards compatibility: if tenant has no config, behave as current router (no caps).
test_plan:
- Unit tests for allocator arithmetic, decay windows, and fallback graph traversal.
- Integration tests that spin up two SKU classes in staging and assert routing decisions under induced eviction signals.
- Chaos tests: simulate spot eviction spikes and confirm fallback events are recorded and tenant-level budget metrics converge.
- Load test: simulate 10k RPS mixed workload and confirm no SLO regressions for priority tenants.
- End-to-end quality check: run prompt evaluation harness to measure quality delta after automated fallback.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flagged rollout to internal tenants (dev accounts) for 2 weeks. 2) Small external beta: opt-in tenants with explicit budget caps and telemetry consent. 3) Expand to more tenants with conservative thresholds and automated A/B quality checks. 4) Full GA when 95% of beta tenants show <5% quality regression and cost savings >12% on average.\nAll stages include kill-switch and automatic reversion on error budget or increased error rate.
acceptance_criteria: Budget-orchestrator service deployed in staging behind FF
Allocator applies per-tenant burst deductions correctly under synthetic load
Router returns SKU and variant decisions with decision-tags visible in traces
Fallback events increment fallback_events metric and visible in console
No regression in p99 latency for P0 tenants during staging chaos test
Documentation page in Console docs describing tenant-level budget controls
